h: Caverns, Fossils and Black Country Character
p: Dudley's Castle Hill sits on a ridge of limestone that shaped the whole town, and once you know that, everything around the zoo starts to make sense. For centuries the limestone was mined from tunnels and caverns beneath the hill, and you can still explore some of them.

Next to the Black Country Living Museum, the Dudley Canal and Tunnel Trust runs boat trips into the Dudley Tunnel and the old limestone mines, gliding through flooded caverns by torchlight. It's an unforgettable experience, and children will talk about it for weeks. Just north of the town centre, the Wren's Nest nature reserve is one of the best-known fossil sites in Britain. It's famous for trilobites, so common here that one, nicknamed the Dudley Bug, features on the town's coat of arms. Bring sharp eyes and you may spot fossils in the loose rocks.

The town centre is a short walk downhill from the zoo, with the shops and markets of a classic Black Country town. Try a few Black Country favourites while you're here; faggots and peas and pork scratchings are local pride and joy.

Getting there: Dudley Zoo is on the edge of the town centre, with buses from Birmingham and Wolverhampton stopping close by. Wear proper shoes and take it steady on the climb up to the castle, but don't skip it. The view is a good reward.
